max-support: Hey team, customer (acct `acme-ml`) is seeing a steady stream of 502/504s against hosted inference since 10:23 UTC after we ran the cert rotate. They report ~40% error rate for generate requests. Logs show a lot of `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and occasional TLS handshake failures. Anyone seen this pattern?

ingrid-plat: saw similar in staging when we changed the cert chain. Quick grep from edge proxy: `grep -c 'upstream prematurely closed' /var/log/nginx/proxy.log` jumped from ~5/hr to ~350 in 10m.

devin-sre: can you paste a sample trace id? Also which frontdoor (us-west-2) and which model route?

max-support: trace ids: `trace=tr-6b2f3a` , `tr-6b2f3b`. Frontdoor: fw-usw2-edge-03. Model route: `/v1/generate?model=redwood-small` (hosted).

sara.ops: paging PD now — customer is actively impacted and their SLAs are hitting. :warning:

pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-198 triggered (priority P1) — assigning oncall.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation completed at 10:21:10 UTC (rotation-id: rot-2026-04-10-03). No other deploys in window.

ingrid-plat: posting a few quick snippets: from nginx error log around a failing request:

```
2026-04-10T10:23:27Z [error] 1234#0: *987654 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.1.45, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2.0", upstream: "http://10.10.4.22:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai", request_id: tr-6b2f3a
```

and from the backend (inference runtime) around same time:

```
2026-04-10T10:23:27Z runtime: connection reset by peer while flushing headers to proxy-tr (tr-6b2f3a)
2026-04-10T10:23:27Z runtime: TLS error: unexpected message (handshake aborted)
```

max-support: repro steps from customer: high concurrency burst (40 req/s) with many streams open (they're using http/2 multiplexing). If I repeat using curl I'm not hitting 100% failures but see occasional 502s.

devin-sre: h2 stream multiplexing + keepalive pool mismatch rings a bell. After cert rotation we restarted nginx frontdoors but not the long-lived upstream worker pools in the runtime, which maintain persistent TLS sessions. If the runtime rotated its certs or reset TLS contexts, connection reuse on the upstream side could break mid-stream leading to resets.

ingrid-plat: config checks: nginx keepalive_timeout is 60s, upstream idle_timeout for the runtime is 30s in envoy config (weird mismatch). Also runtime had a small restart during rotate (killed and rolled over) at 10:21:12 but didn't drain gracefully in one of the pods.

max-support: here's a curl repro I ran from east coast to mimic the customer:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' --http2 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

I get `HTTP/2 502` occasionally and `upstream prematurely closed connection` in logs.

sara.ops: Customer's asks: 1) root cause 2) mitigations now 3) long term fix. Priority P1.

devin-sre: short-term mitigation: 1) force a graceful drain + restart of runtime pods on fw-usw2-edge-03 to clear half-open TLS sessions; 2) toggle nginx `keepalive` to disable upstream connection reuse for the busiest route as a canary (set `keepalive 0` on the `upstream` block for /v1/generate); 3) temporarily route traffic to fw-usw2-edge-04 if capacity allows.

ingrid-plat: I can apply a targeted config change to nginx to disable upstream keepalives for the generate route and reload (non-disruptive). That should stop reuse of possibly-broken TLS connections.

max-support: please do that and let customer know we're trying a config change. I'm collecting timestamps and trace ids.

ingrid-plat: rolling config change to upstream block now (nginx reload) on fw-usw2-edge-03 -> fw-usw2-edge-04 unaffected.

(5m later)
ingrid-plat: reload complete. error rate dropped to ~6% in the last 3m (was ~40%). traces still show a few old trace ids failing.

devin-sre: proceeding to gracefully drain one runtime pod (runtime-pod-07) and restart with drain timeout 60s. Observing logs during drain to ensure inflight completes.

(10m later)
devin-sre: pod drained and restarted cleanly. no crash loops. metrics look stable.

max-support: customer reports error rate ~2% now and can confirm throughput recovered. They're happy with quick mitigation, but want RC. :thumbsup:

sara.ops: next steps (post-mortem): 1) align idle/keepalive timeouts across frontdoor/nginx/envoy/runtime 2) add pre-rotate checklist to drain upstream pools before cert rotations 3) implement a healthcheck that fails open on TLS mismatch so proxy doesn't reuse a broken pool 4) add a canary route for cert rotates to detect this earlier.

ingrid-plat: +1 on pre-rotate drain check. I'll open a GH issue with suggested config diffs and a runbook step.

devin-sre: also recommend a short-term alert: spike in `upstream prematurely closed connection` rate > X in 1m on any frontdoor -> auto-disable keepalive for that route and notify oncall.

max-support: I'll update the customer with the mitigation summary and ETA for a follow-up postmortem. Thanks all.

pagerduty: INC-2026-198 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

sara.ops: filing for postmortem. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
